pairs.subject: selection-score-calibration
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/pipeline-entry-action.ts:587 A command-bar `reject below N%` is sealed as a human `rejected` record (policyVersion "command-bar"), and the clean arm (heldOutEntryIds in decision-record-store.ts:681-682) subtracts only `auto_rejected` records, so a holdout-spared candidate later rejected by a typed score threshold stays in the clean arm as a negative that the score produced.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/pipeline-entry-action.ts:587 Step 9 says the arm is sparings minus later score-caused rejections. This core writes a threshold-driven bulk reject with the human kind, which the arm's subtraction (kind = auto_rejected only) cannot see, so the reject is not removed from the arm.

app/_lib/pipeline-command.ts:114 The command bar picks the rejected set purely by score below a typed cutoff, so it is a score-caused path. Downstream it is not given its own leakage level: it gets the same record kind as a hand reject, and the holdout surface's 'score did NOT mechanically produce their outcome' claim is wrong for these rows.

app/_lib/pipeline-stages.ts:171 The advance-axis positive set (calibrationAdvancedStages) comes from the stage ROLE gate, never from a display name. pipeline-status.ts:41 keeps declined, rematched and role_closed as statuses separate from rejected, so non-merit terminals can be excluded.

pairs.registryProposal: The holdout technique's step 9 says 'minus the set of automated rejections'. It should instead say 'minus every rejection whose target set was selected by the score, including human-confirmed threshold bulk actions'. A recruiter-confirmed 'reject below N%' is exactly the case a kind-based subtraction misses.
